subject.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation

question: Should the macOS Computer Use health repair automatically escalate a scoped child from SIGTERM to SIGKILL after two seconds when the child remains alive?
rationale: This is a deliberate change to the recovery and availability contract, not merely a mechanical implementation detail; source review cannot determine whether preserving a potentially busy MCP child is preferable to forced cleanup.

options.title: Accept bounded forced cleanup
options.body: Approve the SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL contract after redacted macOS app-server evidence shows the scoped repair targets only stale children.

options.title: Keep SIGTERM-only repair
options.body: Retain the existing best-effort termination behavior and pursue diagnostics or an explicit operator-controlled recovery path instead.

options.title: Require opt-in escalation
options.body: Expose forced cleanup only through an explicitly selected recovery action if automatic SIGKILL is too disruptive for the default health path.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded forced cleanup
recommendation.body: Approve the SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL contract after redacted macOS app-server evidence shows the scoped repair targets only stale children.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server lifecycle work makes steipete the best available owner for the recovery-contract decision.
